learningObjective: Understand how graph-level, tensor-expression-level, and loop-level IRs collaborate in a typical deep-learning compiler pipeline.

canonicalClaims.claim: Graph-level IR performs coarse-grained rewrites over atomic ops (fusion, constant folding, shape/layout choices) without exposing loops.
conditions: The graph-level IR treats ops as opaque units with typed inputs/outputs (e.g., HLO, Relax).
nonImplications: Does not imply graph-level fusion is universally superior; it works at coarse granularity.

canonicalClaims.claim: Tensor-expression IR represents per-element computation via structured ops (linalg.generic, TensorIR) and is the natural layer for tiling and hardware-intrinsic mapping.
conditions: The IR supports iteration attributes (indexing maps, iterator types).
nonImplications: Does not imply tensor-expression IR alone yields good performance without downstream loop-level passes.

canonicalClaims.claim: Loop-level IR makes iteration and memory access explicit; it is where unrolling, vectorization, and low-level scheduling apply.
conditions: The IR uses explicit loop constructs (affine, scf, LLVM loops).
nonImplications: Does not imply loop-level IR is always necessary for GPU codegen; some pipelines emit Triton/GPU dialects from tensor form.

misconceptions.claim: Compilers author programs at the loop-level and recover graph structure upward.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The flow is top-down; graph-level is the authoring layer and loops are derived by lowering.

misconceptions.claim: Graph-level IR handles all loop transformations including tiling.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Tiling operates on iteration; it is a tensor- or loop-level transformation.

misconceptions.claim: Loop-level IR is the only layer needed; graph and tensor layers are redundant.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Each layer offers rewrites appropriate to its granularity; graph-level fusion and tensor-level intrinsic mapping cannot be expressed cleanly at the loop layer alone.

misconceptions.claim: The three IR layers must have hard, non-crossable boundaries.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Some pipelines cross layers for iterative refinement (e.g., re-planning after codegen feedback).

performanceScenarios: Each layer contributes complementary optimization opportunities; a good compiler explores all three.
